primary_claim: Distilling paraphrased versions of Claude 3.7 Sonnet's own math scratchpads into its base model yields pass@1 MATH accuracy very close to distilling the original scratchpads, suggesting encoded reasoning / CoT steganography does not play a significant role in this early checkpoint's math performance.

effect.value: distilled-on-paraphrased-scratchpad model performance very close to distilled-on-original-scratchpad model performance

limitations_stated: distilling paraphrased scratchpads may not always remove encoded reasoning, either because the paraphrase does not change the syntax sufficiently or changes it in a reversible way

if the paraphrase changes the text to a style much less common in pretraining, the base model might have a harder time fitting the scratchpads, which may result in lower performance regardless of encoded reasoning

in an exploratory experiment, paraphrasing-style formatting alone (breaking thoughts into <thought></thought> blocks without paraphrasing) dropped pass@1 MATH accuracy by 7%, suggesting distraction effects can confound results
chunked paraphrase results are not exactly comparable to non-chunked results because length filtering was not applied consistently to them
quote: training it to use paraphrased versions of the scratchpads does not degrade performance
